subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does the Gateway security boundary require global rejection of reserved prototype keys even when closed TypeBox schemas and method validators reject unknown fields and no pollution sink has been demonstrated?
rationale: The reported exploit chain is unsupported, but deciding whether to add defense-in-depth rejection across extensible plugin RPC payloads is a security-boundary policy choice rather than a safe automated repair.

options.title: Require focused exploit proof
options.body: Keep the current validation design and close the report if authenticated core and plugin RPC probes show no prototype mutation or unsafe downstream copy sink.

options.title: Add defense-in-depth rejection
options.body: Sponsor a canonical protocol-level reserved-key guard with compatibility analysis and tests across core and plugin RPC payloads.

recommendation.title: Require focused exploit proof
recommendation.body: Keep the current validation design and close the report if authenticated core and plugin RPC probes show no prototype mutation or unsafe downstream copy sink.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway authentication and security-boundary history provides the strongest available routing signal.
